Wald Test of a Parameter Vector

Source: R/wald-wald.R
Wald.Rd

Computes the Wald statistic $$ W = \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} - \boldsymbol{\theta}_{0} \right)^{\prime} \operatorname{Var} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \right)^{-1} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} - \boldsymbol{\theta}_{0} \right) $$ and its \(p\) value from the \(\chi^{2}\) distribution with degrees of freedom equal to the number of parameters. The inverse is computed from the Cholesky factor of var_est.

Usage

Wald(est, var_est, theta = NULL)

Arguments

est

Numeric vector. Vector of parameter estimates (\(\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\)).

var_est

Numeric matrix. Sampling covariance matrix of parameter estimates (\(\operatorname{Var} \left( \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \right)\)), symmetric and positive definite.

theta

Numeric vector. Parameter values when the null hypothesis is true (\(\boldsymbol{\theta}_{0}\)). If NULL, a vector of zeros.

Value

Returns a numeric vector with the following elements:

chisq

Chi-square statistic.

df

Degrees of freedom.

p

p value.

See also

Other Wald Confidence Intervals Functions: CIWald(), ProbsofAlpha()

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
Wald(
  est = coef(fit),
  var_est = vcov(fit),
  theta = NULL
)
#>    chisq       df        p 
#> 2058.832    3.000    0.000
